Byomkesh.description: A renowned detective and truth-seeker known for his sharp intellect and investigative skills who solves complex cases.

Ajit.description: The narrator of the story and Byomkesh's close friend and chronicler. He documents Byomkesh's adventures and assists in investigations.

Ramani Mohan Sanyal.description: A clever and intelligent police inspector who shares a professional rapport with Byomkesh.

Sunil.description: The son of Shiva Prasad Sarkar, initially seen as a spendthrift but revealed to be a cunning mastermind.

Reba.description: Sunil's wife and Shiva Prasad's daughter-in-law, described as an intelligent, practical, and modern-minded woman who inherits the property.

Anna.description: The old woman servant in Sunil and Reba's house, responsible for all housework and cooking. She is considered trustworthy by Reba.

Shiva Prasad Sarkar.description: A wealthy businessman in the liquor trade and father of Sunil who bequeaths his property to Reba.

Hukum Singh.description: A strong young goon and wrestler hired by Sunil to kill Reba, who is eventually killed by his employer.

Mukund Singh.description: Hukum Singh's brother, a goon and wrestler who avenges his brother's death by killing Sunil.

Biren.description: A young policeman and radio operator who sets up the tape-recorder for Byomkesh and Ramani Babu.

Adrishya Trikon.description: The original Bengali title of the chapter, meaning 'The Invisible Triangle.'

Dak bungalow.description: A government guest house, often used for lodging by officials or travelers in India.

Fiat.description: An Italian automobile brand; here it refers to the small car Reba buys after selling the big house.

Bengali.description: Refers to the language and culture of Bengal; Reba is seen reading a Bengali book.

The adventures of Byomkesh Bakshi.description: A book within the story, referencing the exploits of Byomkesh, written by Ajit.

Main police station.description: Refers to the central or principal police station in the town, as opposed to a smaller local station.

Rabindriya.description: Refers to the style of writing associated with Rabindranath Tagore, a famous Bengali poet and writer.

babu.description: A respectful term of address for men in Bengal, often used for educated or official persons.

Daroga.description: A term for a police inspector or officer in India.

photostat.description: An old-fashioned term for a photocopy.

letterhead.description: Paper with a printed heading, often bearing the name and address of a person or organization.

satchel.description: A small bag, often used for carrying documents or equipment.
